boundary_note: Bounded first pass for the frozen Yellow Bayou (Norwood's Plantation) record (May 18, 1864) in the Red River Campaign [March-April 1864]. The frozen campaign label reads March-April 1864 and the live date field reads 'March-April 1864'; neither replaces the record's frozen dates. The May 17 fighting near Moreauville and the May 19-20 crossing of the Atchafalaya are context. Campaign-wide marches, returns, river operations and multi-action loss totals are context; they are not assigned to one record or added across records. Draft claims do not alter model inputs.

claims.rationale: No inspected return establishes matched personnel at a common opening boundary. The frozen side-specific numerical strength bounds are blank (missing_numeric_strength). No figure in this pass is adopted as a simultaneous opening force.

claims.value: The frozen force field reads 1st and 3rd Divisions, XVI Army Corps [US] and District of Western Louisiana [CS]; the live field reads zero. Irwin says A. J. Smith's command held the position near Yellow Bayou when Taylor attacked with his whole force; Taylor's May 19 dispatch says he fought fresh troops recently arrived from Texas. On May 10 Taylor put his own force at scarce 6,000.
claims.rationale: The Union force is identified differently by Irwin and Taylor; the only numerical figure is Taylor's own from eight days earlier. None is adopted as a matched opening strength. The live zero is not measured absence.

claims.value: The frozen result reads Union strategic victory and the live result Union Victory (strategic). Taylor says his men held the field, the enemy falling back at once and leaving 30 dead; Irwin says Mower drove the Confederates off the field in confusion; NPS says the see-saw action ended when the ground cover caught fire and both sides retired.
claims.rationale: Retain the original result and engagement interval; later movements and campaign contribution are different measures. No new probabilities or individual causal credit. The frozen 'strategic' qualifier and NPS's escape statement are campaign context.

claims.value: The frozen casualty text reads 860 total (US 360; CS 500), and the live field agrees. Irwin gives Mower's loss as 38 killed, 226 wounded and 3 missing, 267 in all; Taylor's loss as about 500 by his own report; and 452 killed and wounded by the Confederate returns. Taylor's dispatch puts his loss at 500, with 30 killed, 50 severely wounded and some hundred prisoners.
claims.rationale: Original casualty returns were not inspected; preserve totals, categories, cutoffs and differences. No canonical reconciliation or casualty-based opening count; related actions must not be added without resolving population overlap.

open_questions: A. J. Smith's and Mower's reports (Nos. 30-31), Hill's, Lynch's, Kinney's, Shaw's and the regimental Yellow Bayou reports (Nos. 34, 37-51), Faries's report (No. 103), the Confederate returns cited by Irwin and W. Steele's report remain deferred.

NPS/CWSAC is one family. Richard B. Irwin's History of the Nineteenth Army Corps (Putnam's, 1892) is a retrospective history by the former assistant adjutant-general of the corps and of Banks's Department of the Gulf, an interested Union account; it cites the Official Records and gives Taylor's and Kirby Smith's figures, so it is not independent of them. Taylor's April 18, 1864 report, his March 13-14 letters printed as its inclosures, his April 24-May 19 dispatches and his April 11 general order are one family of interested Confederate accounts. Official Records Series I, Volume XXXIV, Part 1 is a shared container, not an additional witness. Report dates are not event times or proof of contemporary knowledge.
No automatic commander attribution, causal campaign score, morale/readiness number or battle/campaign double counting.
